hints.S39_A1: A DOVE comes out FROM BENEATH A SILK HANDKERCHIEF, to the audience's DELIGHT. Ask: which verb means to make something appear from a hidden place? 'Swallowed' and 'destroyed' would leave no bird at all.
hints.S39_A2: AND REAPPEAR tells you the ball must first go the other way. Ask: which verb means to disappear suddenly and completely? 'Grow', 'expand' and 'bounce' all keep the ball firmly in sight.
hints.S39_A3: The magician WALKED THROUGH A SOLID GLASS PANEL, and the audience GASPED. Ask: which noun names the shock of seeing something that cannot possibly be real? Boredom and anger never make a crowd gasp.
hints.S39_A4: The magician ASKED FOR somebody FROM THE AUDIENCE to help with his NEXT TRICK. Ask: which noun names a person who steps forward willingly? 'Enemy' and 'suspect' would turn a helper into a threat.
hints.S39_A5: The purpose is stated: SO THEY MISS THE REAL TRICK, using PATTER AND MOVEMENT. Ask: which verb means to pull attention away from what matters? 'Educates' and 'rewards' would help the audience, not fool them.
hints.S39_B1: EVERY YEAR marks a habit, so the tense stays present. The subject is THE SCHOOL - one thing, however many students it holds. Ask: does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S39_B2: The whole sentence is a finished story: he LOCKED IT SHUT WITH A GOLDEN KEY. Ask: what is the past form of this irregular verb? Adding -ed would produce a word that does not exist.
hints.S39_B3: THAN sets this show against THE ONE WE SAW AT THE SCHOOL CARNIVAL - exactly two shows. Ask: for two, comparative or superlative? And can a four-syllable adjective ever take -er? 'Excitinger' is not English.
hints.S39_B4: Every trick in that show is in this race, not merely two of them. Ask: for three or several, do you need a comparative or a superlative? And IMPRESSIVE is long, so no -er ending can rescue you here.
hints.S39_B5: Two clues. A LITTLE SPACE is one uncountable amount, not a set of countable things, and SOME STUDENTS SAT FURTHER BACK - it is over and done. Ask: which form of 'be' is both singular and past?
hints.S39_B6: JUST tips you off: neither performance beat the other. Ask: which pair holds two things at exactly equal level? 'Less … than' would demote one, and 'the most … of' needs three or several.
hints.S39_B7: THREE VOLUNTEERS did nothing themselves - BY THE MAGICIAN names who acted on them, and it is finished. Ask: which choice is passive and past, and does a plural subject take 'was' or its plural partner?
hints.S39_B8: TOLD THE AUDIENCE = reported speech, and this is a warning against being TOO LOUD. Ask: after 'told' + person, which verb form follows? And where does a negative word stand - in front of that infinitive, or inside it?
hints.S39_C1: ENJOYS is the deciding word: some verbs demand the -ing form and refuse an infinitive. Ask: do you say 'enjoy to read' or 'enjoy reading'? Copy that same pattern here.
hints.S39_C2: EVERY EVENING sets a habit, and HE is one person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s? A past form would clash with his nightly routine.
hints.S39_C3: LAST FRIDAY is finished time, and it happened once - FOR THE VERY FIRST TIME. Ask: which form is simple past? A continuous form would claim the show was still running around some other event.
hints.S39_C4: WHILE means one action had already begun when A DOVE APPEARED and cut across it. Ask: which form shows a past action still in progress? Leo is one person, so pick the singular helper, not the plural one.
hints.S39_C5: HIS FRIENDS is plural, and they had their eyes on it AT THAT VERY MOMENT, FROM DIFFERENT ANGLES. Ask: which form shows a past action still in progress, and which helper belongs with a plural subject?
hints.S39_C6: WANTS refuses an -ing form after it. Ask: do you say 'she wants going', or 'she wants ___ go' with a small word slipped in front? Fill that same little word in before he TURNS TWELVE.
hints.S39_C7: SHOULD is a modal, and a modal is always followed by a bare verb - no -s, no -ing, no infinitive marker. Ask: which single box form is the plain, unchanged verb? EVERYONE does not alter it either.
hints.S39_C8: RIGHT NOW means at this very moment, so the action must be in progress. Ask: which form shows something happening as we speak? Leo counts as one person, so choose the singular helper, not 'are'.
hints.S39_D1: The dash defines it: MOVE OBJECTS WITH THE FINGERS SO QUICKLY that THE EYE CANNOT FOLLOW. Ask: which box word completes the fixed phrase '___ OF HAND'? It names the skill itself, not the trick's effect.
hints.S39_D2: The example spells it out: A DRAMATIC GESTURE WITH ONE HAND DRAWS THE EYES while the other hand works in secret. Ask: which box word names the art of steering attention AWAY from the real action?
hints.S39_D3: The dash explains it: A FALSE IMAGE THAT THE BRAIN ACCEPTS AS REAL. Note 'an' in front of the gap - the word must begin with a vowel sound. Ask: which box word names that false picture in the mind?
hints.S39_D4: Every one of them sits IN THE AUDIENCE and FEELS AS THOUGH THE IMPOSSIBLE has just happened. Ask: which box word names one single person who watches a show? A skill or a false image cannot feel anything.
hints.S39_D5: AT THE END OF SOME SHOWS the magician gives the secret away, and audiences are SURPRISED at how simple the method is. Ask: which box word is the verb meaning to make a hidden thing known? It follows 'choose to'.
hints.S39_E1: The underlined word is meant to say 'excessively': the trick moved FAST for anyone to FOLLOW WITH THEIR EYES. Ask: which spelling means 'more than enough'? It carries one extra letter.
hints.S39_E2: WATCHED is the action, and the underlined word tells you HOW the class watched. Ask: which two letters must be added before an adjective may describe a verb? On its own, an adjective can describe only a noun.
hints.S39_E3: HALFS is the trap: nouns ending in -f seldom take a plain -s. Ask: how do you write more than one leaf, or more than one loaf? Apply that same swap to this word.
hints.S39_E4: The subject is THE AUDIENCE MEMBERS - many people, not one crowd-word. Ask: does a plural subject take 'was', or its plural partner? Count the people, not the group noun standing beside them.
hints.S39_E5: AMAZINGER piles an -er ending onto an adjective that already has MORE in front of it. Ask: which of those two must go? A long adjective takes a helper word, never an ending - and never both together.
hints.S39_F1: Two things happen at once: your eyes lock onto the RIGHT HAND while the LEFT HAND works unseen. Ask: after 'As', which half comes first - the looking, or the missing? A comma then joins them.
hints.S39_F2: 'Unless' is a two-in-one word: it already contains a hidden negative. Ask: which half sets the condition - PAY ATTENTION, or being TRICKED EVERY SINGLE TIME? And what tense follows 'unless' - present, or future with 'will'?
